title: Single-arm pilot study for assessing usability and acceptance of an mHealth app for the prevention and management of performance-related pain in musicians.
summary: Up to 80 % of musicians experience acute or chronic playing-related pain at some point in their lives. This makes pain the most common reason why musicians seek medical care. It has been shown that digital health services, such as health apps, help patients with chronic pain to find out about evidence-based health topics and lead a healthier lifestyle, and can therefore help them to manage persistent pain. We have developed the ‘Crescendo’ app for musicians to help prevent the onset of pain or to manage persistent pain.  Music students and professional musicians are invited to test the app for four weeks and then share their experiences and impressions of the app via online interviews and questionnaires. We want to use these to find out how useful, user-friendly, and appealing the app is to musicians. We’d also like to find out what they like about the app and what they think could be improved.
conditions: Chronic pain disorder with somatic and psychological factors

interventions.name: Intervention group - Music students and professional musicians both with and without pain—will use the Crescendo app over four weeks for the prevention or managment of performance-related pain.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Fluent in English or German language
Professional musician* or music student currently enrolled in a degree at a higher education music institution
Is an instrumentalist

*Professional musician is defined as someone who 1) has a musical degree and is currently active (plays at least 3 times a week on average) OR 2) does not have a musical degree but is currently employed by a professional ensemble
Exclusion criteria:
With acute musculoskeletal injury (not performance-related)
AND/OR acute psychiatric or chronic neurological disorders
Pregnancy
Type I and II Diabetes
